beats.narration_text: Crypto markets never close — no opening bell, no closing bell, no pause. I'm Anjana. Here's why that broke the old model of human trading hours, and why the only thing that can actually watch a market that never sleeps turns out to be a machine.

show.event: ClaudeComposerAsk: greeting 'Hello, Anjana'; ask types itself
runningText 'mapping the markets…'
output lines resolve: 'three cities, one machine watching all of them' / 'the closing bell breaks — 24/7, no pause' / 'reaction time: 0.003s'

props.segment: AI Doesn't Sleep, Markets Don't Wait
props.command: Crypto markets never close — no opening bell, no closing bell, just continuous trading forever. Can you show me why that broke the old model of human trading hours, and why AI ends up being the only thing that can actually watch a market that never sleeps?
output: three cities, one machine watching all of them
the closing bell breaks — 24/7, no pause

beats.narration_text: Right now, somewhere in the world, a market is moving. A token is crashing in Seoul. A contract is liquidating in London. A whale is buying in New York. And nobody is watching all of it at once. Except the machines.

show.event: dark stage; a stylized globe fades in, slowly rotating
Seoul pulses red, small price chart dropping — on 'crashing in Seoul'
London pulses amber, liquidation bar draining — on 'liquidating in London'
New York pulses green, volume spike — on 'buying in New York'
human silhouettes at each city dim to 20%; a central AI node fades in, bright, all trade lines reroute through it — on 'except the machines'

beats.narration_text: For a hundred years, markets had opening bells and closing bells. Traders worked the floor from nine to four, went home, and the world paused. Then crypto arrived, and the clock broke. Bitcoin trades at three AM on a Sunday. Ethereum moves on holidays. There is no closing bell anymore.

show.event: classic analog wall clock, 'MARKET OPEN' green bar spanning 9:30–4:00, ticking normally
a crack appears at 12 o'clock — on 'then crypto arrived'
crack spreads, glass shatters outward in slow motion
behind the broken clock: a seamless 24-hour glowing ring, BTC/ETH icons orbiting
label lands: '24/7/365. No closing bell.'

beats.narration_text: A human trader needs sleep. Eight hours off the screen every night. Weekends. Vacations. Blinks, bathroom breaks, a moment of distraction. In a market that never pauses, every second you are not watching is a second something can move against you. One flash crash at two AM and your position is gone before your alarm goes off.

show.event: split screen: left — person at a desk, green 'ACTIVE' badge; right — continuous candlestick chart
a clock fast-forwards through the day above the left side
person pushes back, walks off; badge flips red 'OFFLINE'; monitors dim — on 'weekends, vacations'
a sharp red candle drops at 2:14 AM on the right side — flash crash
a phone lights up on the nightstand: 'POSITION LIQUIDATED' — person still asleep

props.sparkLine: The market doesn't wait for you.

beats.narration_text: AI does not sleep. It watches ten thousand pairs across a hundred exchanges simultaneously. It reads the order book, scans social sentiment, tracks whale wallets, monitors liquidation cascades, and reacts in milliseconds. Not because it is smarter than you. Because it is always there. The edge is not intelligence. The edge is presence.

show.event: a central AI node pulses; six data streams begin radiating outward
Order Books stream activates — scrolling bid/ask numbers
Social Sentiment stream activates — tweet-like snippets
Whale Wallets stream activates — wallet fragments + $ amounts
Liquidation Maps stream activates — heat-map cells flashing
News Feeds + On-Chain Data streams activate — headlines, block hashes
decision output cycles 'BUY / HOLD / EXIT'; ms counter ticking in the corner
all six streams pulse simultaneously, node glows bright, counter freezes at '0.003s' — on 'the edge is presence'

beats.narration_text: Markets don't wait for you to wake up. They don't care about your time zone, your schedule, or your sleep. AI doesn't need any of those things. That is not the future. That is Tuesday.

show.event: the globe from B01 returns — same rotation, same cities, same trade lines; human silhouettes gone, AI node already centered
globe dims slightly — on 'not the future'
title lands, large and still: 'AI Doesn't Sleep.' / 'Markets Don't Wait.' — on 'Tuesday'

beats.narration_text: Let's recap with Claude. Crypto broke the closing bell — markets run twenty-four seven, three sixty-five. A human trader still needs sleep, weekends, a break. AI watches thousands of pairs across hundreds of exchanges at once, reacting in milliseconds. The edge isn't intelligence. It's presence.

show.event: 0.5s lead pause, then ClaudeVerdictArtifact card builds in
line 1: cracked-clock icon settles in
line 2: sleeping-person icon settles in
line 3: AI-node icon settles in
line 4: 'presence' locks in, largest element

beats.narration_text: Your turn. "I have a task at work that quietly runs on its own schedule, whether I'm watching or not — a queue, a system, a process that can go wrong at 2 AM just as easily as 2 PM. Can you help me: one, figure out which parts of it genuinely need round-the-clock presence versus just a fast reaction during my own working hours; two, design one simple always-on check — an alert, a script, a monitor — that covers the real gap; and three, tell me honestly whether automating that presence is worth it, or whether I'm solving a problem I don't actually have?" Paste that into Claude and find out if your own blind spot is worth watching — or if the market analogy doesn't actually hold for you.

show.event: ClaudeComposerAsk: greeting 'Your turn.'; prompt types itself into the composer
runningText 'checking your own blind spot…'
